messages:
maria: heads-up - we got a customer report that their rerank calls are getting 429s even though they’re under overall quota. seems tied to our per-second rate cap on the ranking envelope.
ajay: can you paste the request shape? wondering if the new `candidates` array blew up token counting or parallel fanout.
maria: sample payload they used: ```json
{
  \"query\": \"how to set up x\",
  \"candidates\": [{\"id\":1,\"text\":\"...\"}, {\"id\":2,\"text\":\"...\"}],
  \"features\": {\"user_tier\": \"pro\"}
}
```
li: quick note — our ratecap math counts `score_units` where each candidate triggers a score call. if a request asks for `top_k`=50 and we fan out to 3 models (scoring + fallback + diversity) that’s 150 score-units.
sophie: ugh. customers assume rerank is 1 request = 1 unit. we need clearer UX in Console + API docs.
ajay: ops question: should we change server behavior or change telemetry + console to show per-request estimated units? my bias is UI first (less blast radius).
maria: agree, update console first. display an "Estimated Score Units" before you click send + inline warning when candidate_count * model_fanout > 1000.
console-bot: deploy scheduled: feature/estimated-units-preview -> staging at 12:30 UTC (automated) :deploy:
li: also want to raise that our fallback model selection (fast-rank) currently runs when latency > 400ms or queue depth threshold hit. that can double units unexpectedly. we should show which model will be used in the console during canary rollouts.
ajay: technically we can expose `routing_hint` in example payloads and Console can toggle it. e.g. `routing_hint: \"low_latency\"` picks the lighter model.
maria: proposal: API returns an envelope with `estimated_units`, `model_plan` and then `scores`. sample response: ```json
{
  \"estimated_units\": 120,
  \"model_plan\": [\"scorer-v2\", \"fallback-fast-rank\"],
  \"scores\": [{\"id\":1,\"score\":0.81}]
}
```
sophie: yes please. product needs that to show cost impact per route and to teach customers cheaper options.
li: caveat — adding `model_plan` leaks internal model names; maybe show abstract labels: `primary/latency-optimized` rather than `scorer-v2`.
ajay: fine, return `model_plan` as friendly tags and `opaque_ids` for mapping in telemetry. e.g. `\{"model_plan\": [\"primary\", \"fallback\"], \"model_ids\": [\"m-42\"]\}`.
maria: follow-up: quota enforcement. We should avoid surprising 429s mid-request. Can we reserve capacity on accept or do soft-throttles with partial success?
li: server-side reservation is expensive. alternative: accept request, best-effort score up to a per-request cap, and include `truncated: true` in envelope + `remaining_units_needed` in response. customer can retry.
ajay: that's good for UX. but need to document billing semantics (do we bill partial?).
sophie: billing: bill for units consumed, and surface an audit when truncated. ops wants explicit log so support can reconcile.
console-bot: note: canary rollout for `estimated-units` UI will include opt-in telemetry flag `rerank_unit_breakdown` for 10% of orgs.
maria: next steps: (1) AJ to PR API response envelope change (friendly model tags + estimated_units + truncated metadata) (2) LI to add truncated logs + telemetry mapping (3) SOPHIE to update Console copy + add warning tooltip about candidate fanout.
ajay: will open PR and include migration notes. will keep envelope fields optional for now to avoid breaking SDKs.
li: I'll add an internal dashboard card: per-route median units, truncated rate, and common fallback patterns. aim to have initial charts in 3 days.
sophie: I'll draft copy and a short in-app banner for early adopters.
maria: thanks team. let's monitor staging signals after console deploy. if 429s persist we revisit server-side reservation. :thumbsup:
